title: Senior Legal Counsel, North America
locations: Chicago, Illinois, US; <span class="jobGeoLocationPin glyphicon glyphicon-map-marker icon-map-marker" aria-hidden="true">
description:
COFCO International is a global agri-business with a clear vision, strong values and a positive culture, focused on being a leader in the global grains, oilseeds and sugar supply chains. We provide the food the world needs in a responsible way. Headquartered is Geneva, Switzerland, we are ambitious, with the right structures and culture to meet the world's increasing and changing needs. With 11,000+ people in 35 countries, our global portfolio includes assets across the Americas, Europe, Africa, Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We trade with over 50 nations, while providing farmers unique direct access to the growing Chinese market.

Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Legal Counsel to support the North America Region of COFCO International. The role will provide comprehensive legal advice and support on corporate and secretarial matters, entity governance, and commercial legal issues affecting the U.S.  and Mexico businesses. The ideal candidate will have 7+ years of post-qualification experience, with exposure to the agricultural commodities or trading industry highly desirable.

This role will act as a key legal business partner, ensuring compliance with U.S. and Mexico corporate requirements while supporting strategic initiatives across the North America region.

Key Responsibilities

• Corporate Governance & Secretarial

• Manage corporate governance matters for the U.S. and Mexico entities, including board meetings, resolutions, and statutory filings.

• Ensure compliance with all federal and state regulations related to corporate structure and governance.

• Maintain corporate records and liaise with external corporate agents as required.

• Legal Advisory & Business Partnering

• Provide legal advice on commercial contracts, corporate law, and regulatory matters relevant to the agricultural commodities industry.

• Support business teams on structuring and negotiating agreements, including supply, distribution, and joint ventures.

• Advise on cross-border transactions, working closely with global legal colleagues.

• Risk Management & Compliance

• Monitor and advise on legal risks associated with business operations in the U.S. and Mexico

• Support compliance with applicable laws, including trade, anti-bribery, sanctions, and data protection.

• Assist in implementing and maintaining internal policies and procedures to mitigate legal risk.

• Collaboration & Representation

• Work closely with global legal teams to align on international corporate governance and reporting requirements.

• Engage with external counsel for specialist advice, managing costs and ensuring high-quality output.

• Act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership and business stakeholders within the U.S. and Mexico entity.

Qualifications & Experience

• J.D. degree from a recognized U.S. law school and admission to practice law in Illinois (or ability to qualify as in-house counsel).

• Minimum 7 years’ post-qualification experience, with a blend of law firm and in-house experience preferred.

• Strong expertise in corporate law, governance, and secretarial matters; additional experience in commercial contracts is a plus.

• Experience in the agricultural, commodity trading, food, or energy industries highly desirable.

• Solid understanding of U.S. corporate regulatory frameworks, with exposure to cross-border transactions.

• Excellent communication, drafting, and negotiation skills.

• Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, and provide pragmatic legal solutions in a fast-paced, international environment.

What We Offer

• Opportunity to join a leading global agri-business with strong growth ambitions.

• Exposure to a diverse and international working environment.

• A role that combines corporate governance with strategic legal advisory work.

• Competitive compensation and benefits package.

COFCO International is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law.

title: Head of Compliance for North America and Derivatives
description:
COFCO International is a global agri-business with a clear vision, strong values and a positive culture, focused on being a leader in the global grains, oilseeds and sugar supply chains. We provide the food the world needs in a responsible way. Headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, we are ambitious, with the right structures and culture to meet the world's increasing and changing needs. With 12,000+ people in 35 countries, our global portfolio includes assets across the Americas, Europe, Africa, Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We trade with over 50 nations, while providing farmers unique direct access to the growing Chinese market.

We are seeking a highly experienced and strategic Head of North America Compliance, with a particular emphasis on commodity derivatives trading both on US and non-US exchanges while enabling responsible growth and operational excellence and acting as a key contact for the US regulators. Reporting directly to CIL’s Chief Compliance Officer

Key responsibilities:

• Develop, lead, and maintain a comprehensive compliance program tailored to the regulatory frameworks governing agricultural commodity derivatives trading.

• Serve as the primary compliance subject matter expert on rules and regulations applicable to the trading of commodity derivatives by monitoring and interpreting U.S. and international regulatory developments and analyzing their impacts on the company

• Promote a strong Compliance culture across commercial and support functions by designing and implementing accessible and readily usable internal policies and procedures, and by providing regular training sessions.

• Conduct periodic risk assessments and controls to ensure that operations and transactions meet local, national and international laws, regulations and business practices (e.g. monitoring position limits, hedge exemptions, preventing or detecting manipulative practices or ensuring that regulatory reporting is complete, accurate and timely sent)

• Collaborate with trading, operations, legal, and IT teams to ensure compliance requirements are integrated into business systems and workflows.

• Advise Senior Management and Traders on CFTC and exchanges rules, compliance matters related to new products, as well as anti-bribery and corruption matters.

• Understand and reflect regulatory considerations arising from commercial strategies, identify and coordinate/assist on projects with compliance related matters and issues.

• Liaise with regulatory bodies to ensure proactive alignment and reporting and ensure investigations and requests from regulators and exchanges are processed appropriately and in a timely manner (centralize regulatory correspondences, obtain required information from relevant departments, draft responses, ensure they are sent in time and inform Management).

• Maintain and develop constant and fluent contacts with market authorities, trade associations and other compliance officers in the industry to ensure alignment of compliance approaches, exert proper influence and be proactive in anticipating changes impacting the business.

• Proactively participate in the global compliance program, coordinating all compliance matters for North America (including ABC, AML and trade sanctions) and all derivatives matters across all countries (involving other compliance teams when necessary)

• Assist the Chief Compliance Officer with the global compliance program and work closely with other compliance teams.

What does it take to be successful in this role:

• 10+ years Compliance experience, ideally in an international commodity trading house and with deep knowledge of commodity derivatives-related regulations.

• Experience in building and enhancing compliance and ethics programs to reduce regulatory risks.

• Proven record of creating compliance partnerships with business management.

• Prior experience working with commodity trading companies.

• Relevan education (min. Bachelor´s Degree).

• Candidates with legal experience, education or training will be highly regarded but not essential.

• Ability to work independently while fostering strong cross-functional collaboration.

• Exceptional regulatory interpretation

• Strong attention to detail with good written skills for policy and reporting requirements

title: Global Cotton Controller
locations: Sao Paulo, São Paulo, BR; <span class="jobGeoLocationPin glyphicon glyphicon-map-marker icon-map-marker" aria-hidden="true">
description:
Com mais de 12 mil colaboradores em 36 países, a COFCO International é uma plataforma de agronegócios da COFCO Corporation, uma das maiores companhias agrícolas e de alimentos da China, com atuação global.

A companhia está acelerando seu crescimento para criar uma cadeia de suprimentos agrícolas de excelência, ancorada na China e competitiva em escala global.

The position is responsible for provide leadership for accounting and reporting for Global Cotton division. Ensure the integrity of its financial results (both in local and IFRS standards), following corporate policies and guidelines. Act as business partner with traders and other team members in supporting Cotton Business to achieve its goals, by providing a financial approach to identify, assessing and mitigating risks while contributing to the effectiveness and efficiency of operations. Engage with functions and regional leaders to ensure Cotton business is properly managed and controlled in all countries. This position will report directly to the Global Controller for Softs, the role offers broad exposure to commercial, operational, and corporate leadership teams. The position may be based in either São Paulo or Santos, Brazil.

Responsibilities
Business Partnership & Strategic Support

• Serve as a trusted financial advisor to senior business leaders and functional stakeholders for local and global business.

• Partner with commercial and operational teams to support strategic and tactical decision-making.

• Provide financial insights to evaluate business opportunities, risks, and performance drivers.

• The role is pivotal for answering questions on a day-to-day basis about various topics.

• Facilitate collaboration between finance and business functions across regions.

• Act as a strong participant of the softs finance leadership team.

Financial Reporting Management

• Responsible for all financial aspects of the Cotton business transactions in the country where the individual is located (e.g., Brazil).

• Participate and manage the preparation of financial statements in accordance with IFRS.

• Perform detailed review of balance sheet and P&L to ensure compliance with Group reporting requirements. Update monthly balance sheet accounts analysis and provide commentary to Senior Management on monthly results for all regions included on the Global business.

• Ensure accuracy of the information in the Accounting Systems consistent with the Trading System.

• Work closely with market risk to assess the mark-to-market pricing against observable market data. Review and document physical inventory, equity, and open contract mark-to-market reports.

• Ensure all Legal Entities maintain reporting structure to be aligned with Global business needs.

Financial Governance & Controls

• Ensure the integrity, consistency, and reliability of financial information.

• Maintain effective financial controls and governance practices.

• Support compliance with applicable accounting standards, internal policies, and regulatory requirements, not limited to the finance function.

• Coordinate internal and external audit activities when required.

• Monitor financial processes and identify opportunities to strengthen controls and efficiency.

• Act as a leader to ensure the business operates under the pre-defined control framework, assisting leaders to revise control activities and to address and immediately communicate issues.

• Oversight/Responsibility of the daily processes reporting to group: global P&L and Position, ensuring month end accounting P&L results are reconciled to the Trade estimate.

• Work collaboratively with the functional support groups to ensure adequate controls through the trade initiation to cash process and straight through processing to the ledger where possible.

Planning, Forecasting & Budgeting

• Develop policies and procedures for the business to be followed in all countries.

• Coordinate annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range planning processes.

• Support the development of business plans and financial targets.

• Monitor performance against budget and forecast, identifying risks and opportunities.

• Ensure the business the working capital usage aligns with corporate requirements in each region and its implication to the Legal Entities capital structure.

• Provide detailed month-end analysis of the individual trade desks to FP&A and Strategy teams.

• Adhoc analysis of significant P&L moves of the business.

• Perform scenario analysis and support strategic planning initiatives.

• Develop recommendations to improve business performance and resource allocation.

• Support the preparation of presentations and reporting materials for senior management.

• Work closely with other regions to drive consistency in the group.

Process Improvement & Transformation

• Drive initiatives focused on process optimization, automation, and operational efficiency.

• Promote standardization of financial reporting and management processes.

• Support finance transformation projects and continuous improvement initiatives.

• Develop scalable reporting solutions that enhance business visibility and decision-making.

• Encourage the adoption of best practices across regions and teams.

Experience

• Significant experience in Finance, Business Controlling, Commercial Finance, FP&A, Accounting, or related finance leadership roles.Proven track record operating within large, complex, and multinational organizations.

• Strong experience partnering with senior business stakeholders.

• Experience supporting fast-paced commercial environments and performance-driven organizations.

• Exposure to global operations and multi-country business structures.

• Proven experience in trading accounting, preferable in Softs commodity.

Technical Expertise

• Strong knowledge of financial reporting, management accounting, and business performance management.Advanced analytical and financial modelling capabilities.

• Experience leading budgeting, forecasting, and planning processes.

• Solid understanding of IFRS or equivalent reporting frameworks.

• Experience working with ERP systems and financial reporting tools.

• Ability to translate complex financial information into clear business insights.

Leadership & Personal Attributes

• Strong business acumen and commercial mindset.Excellent communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills.

• Ability to influence and challenge constructively across all levels of the organization.

• Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities.

• High level of ownership, accountability, and integrity.

• Ability to manage multiple priorities in a dynamic and evolving environment.

• Collaborative leadership style with experience working across different cultures and geographies.

• Continuous improvement mindset with a focus on operational excellence.

Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.Professional accounting qualification (CPA, ACCA, CIMA, CMA, or equivalent) is considered an advantage.
